Stephen accused Formosus of perjury and of having acceded to the papacy illegally.  At the end of the trial, Formosus was pronounced guilty and his papacy retroactively declared null.

He was the first pope of the Byzantine Papacy allowed to be consecrated by the Byzantine Emperor without prior consent, and the first in a line of ten consecutive popes of Eastern origin.  His papacy was marked by reconciliation between the city of Rome and the Empire.

This supposed second John XIV never existed, rather he was confused with a certain cardinal deacon John, son of Robert, who was opposed to Boniface VII and is now excluded from the papal lists.
Pope John VII | Pope John VII (Latin: "Ioannes VII" ; c. 650 – 18 October 707) was Pope from 1 March 705 to his death in 707.  The successor of John VI, he was (like his predecessor) of Greek ancestry.  He is one of the popes of the Byzantine Papacy.
